adi_assessment.authority: EFSA 2011 (group ADI, thay the JECFA 160-200mg/kg rieng le cu)
adi_assessment.source_locator: EFSA Journal 2011;9(3):2004, DOI 10.2903/j.efsa.2011.2004. Group ADI 300 mg/kg bw/day cho ca 4 loai caramen (E150a-d), dua tren NOAEL 30g/kg (nghien cuu 13 tuan tren chuot) + he so an toan 100. LUU Y: EFSA canh bao E150a va E150d co the VUOT group ADI nay o mot so nhom tieu thu; danh gia phoi nhiem lai nam 2012 cho thay khong vuot. CAP NHAT: thay gia tri JECFA cu (160-200mg/kg, rieng cho tung loai) bang group ADI EFSA 2011 moi hon.
adi_assessment.review_note: Verified against primary EFSA/JECFA source on 2026-10-31 (batch 2). Re-check periodically for newer re-evaluations.

allergen_assessment.note: Caramel Class IV (ammonia-sulfite process) may contain residual sulfites as a manufacturing by-product. The caramel additive itself is not a primary allergen, but if SO₂ carry-over in the final food product reaches ≥10 mg/kg, sulfite allergen labeling is triggered under Codex CXS 1-1985 and EU 1333/2008 carry-over limits. Product-level sulfite testing is required; cannot be determined from additive code alone.

sources.locator: IARC Monographs Vol. 101 classifies 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI) as Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic to humans) — evidence from lung tumours in mice; not in rats; genotoxicity data largely negative. E150d (Class IV, sulfite-ammonia caramel) produces 4-MEI as a manufacturing by-product of carbohydrate heating with sulfite + ammonium compounds. EU Regulation 1333/2008 sets maximum 4-MEI limits for Classes III and IV. California Prop 65 requires warning for beverages yielding > 29 μg 4-MEI equivalent/day. FDA position: typical dietary exposure far below tumour-causing doses in rodents.
